# MEMORANDUM

**To:** [Supervising Partner]
**From:** [Associate]
**Date:** November 10, 2026
**Re:** Bredeix Organic Creamery, LLC / Laipeisk Systems, Inc.: risk review of HerdLedger license package and recommended pushback

---

## I. Summary

I reviewed all four documents in the folder:

- the Software License and Services Agreement effective April 1, 2025 (the **Agreement**);
- Statement of Work No. 2 dated September 15, 2026 (the **SOW**);
- the Data Processing Addendum effective April 1, 2025 (the **DPA**); and
- Halverston Risk Partners' October 26, 2026 cover letter enclosing Laipeisk's certificate of insurance (the **COI Letter**).

I found four issues. They are ranked below by how much they matter to Bredeix.

| Rank | Issue | Location | Why it ranks here |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | DPA puts data-breach liability back under the 12-month-fees cap | DPA §8.1 (with Agreement §§1.3, 11.2, 11.3(c)) | Largest potential dollar exposure. Hits sensitive bank and tax data of farmer-suppliers. Gets worse once Phase 2 ACH payments go live. |
| 2 | Pending parent sale to Northfold is an unconsented Change of Control | Agreement §16.2 (facts at SOW §1.2(b)–(c)) | Closing is expected Q1 2027. Without consent, Laipeisk can terminate the core procurement and producer-pay system on 30 days' notice. Time-critical. |
| 3 | Phase 1 Rejection Notice was sent after the 10-day window | SOW §2.2; Agreement §6.2 | Live dispute over deemed acceptance of defective software and the Phase 1 milestone fee. Still actionable because Bredeix reserved its rights. |
| 4 | Automatic five-year renewals with a 30-day opt-out window | Agreement §14.2 | Lock-in risk that grows with the Northfold integration. The first window is about 13 months away. |

The COI Letter appears to be a compliant deliverable and raises no independent issue (Part III). It does give us useful leverage on Issue 1.

**Points needing a client call before we respond to Laipeisk** are flagged in each issue and collected in Part IV.

---

## II. Issues (ranked)

### Issue 1: The DPA pulls data-breach liability back under the cap

**Location:** DPA §8.1. It interacts with Agreement §1.3 (Order of Precedence), §11.2 (Cap) and §11.3(c) (exclusion for Section 9 breaches).

**What the documents say**

- **Agreement §11.2:** each party's aggregate liability is capped at "the Fees paid by Licensee in the 12 months preceding the claim" (the **Cap**).
- **Agreement §11.3(c):** a breach of Section 9 (Confidentiality and Data Security) is excluded from the Cap. This is the uncapped data-security protection Bredeix bargained for.
- **DPA §8.1:** "*Notwithstanding Section 11.3(c) of the Agreement*, each party's aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Addendum, including any Personal Data Breach, *shall be subject to the Cap*."
- **Agreement §1.3:** the order of precedence is "the DPA (as to Personal Data), then this License Agreement, then any Statement of Work."

**Analysis**

Because the DPA prevails over the Agreement as to Personal Data under §1.3, DPA §8.1 controls. Liability for a Personal Data Breach is therefore capped at roughly one year's fees, notwithstanding §11.3(c). Two further consequences follow:

- **Breach costs are capped too.** DPA §7.5 obliges Laipeisk to reimburse notification, call-center, 24 months of credit monitoring and forensic costs. Those reimbursement obligations "arise out of or relate to" the DPA, so they now count against the same Cap.
- **The override may reach further than §11.3(c).** DPA §8.1 caps "aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Addendum," and DPA §8.2 applies Agreement §11 only "except as stated in Section 8.1." Laipeisk could argue that a data incident caused by its gross negligence or willful misconduct (Agreement §11.3(b)) is also capped when it arises under the DPA. We should close that argument off as well.

The clause reads as mutual, but the mutuality is illusory. Only Laipeisk processes Personal Data (DPA §2.1; Annex 1). In practice the clause protects Laipeisk alone.

**Why it matters to Bredeix**

- **The data is highly sensitive.** HerdLedger holds Bredeix's farmer-supplier master file. Under DPA Annex 1 this includes taxpayer identification numbers, bank account and routing numbers, payment, premium and deduction records, and organic certification records. Most of this is "private information" under the New York SHIELD Act (N.Y. Gen. Bus. Law §§899-aa, 899-bb). Because Bredeix sources from Vermont producers, the Vermont Security Breach Notice Act (9 V.S.A. §2435) applies too.
- **Phase 2 increases the exposure.** It adds producer payment processing, NACHA-format ACH files and positive-pay files (SOW §§3.2(b)–(c), 9). A breach could lead to diverted producer payments or ACH fraud, not just exposed records.
- **The costs fall on Bredeix.** As data owner, Bredeix bears the notification obligations, regulator exposure and producer claims. Notification and credit-monitoring costs alone for a full producer base could exceed a year's subscription fees.
- **Producer trust is commercially critical.** For a creamery that depends on its farmer-supplier base, a breach of producers' banking data is a relationship and supply risk, not just a legal one.
- **The Cap may be small when it matters.** It is measured by fees paid in the 12 months before the claim. If milestone fees are disputed or withheld, the Cap could be thin at exactly the wrong time.

**Recommended fix**

Strike DPA §8.1 and conform DPA §8.2 so that Personal Data Breach liability remains uncapped, consistent with Agreement §11.3(c).

If the DPA has already been executed (it bears an April 1, 2025 effective date), this requires a written amendment signed by both parties under DPA §12.3. If it has not been executed, Bredeix should not sign it in its current form.

*Proposed replacement language (DPA §8):*

> **8.1 Liability.** Section 11 of the Agreement, including Section 11.3, applies to liability arising out of or relating to this Addendum. For clarity, (a) any breach of this Addendum by Licensor or its Subprocessors, and any Personal Data Breach caused by Licensor or its Subprocessors, constitutes a breach of Section 9 of the Agreement for purposes of Section 11.3(c) of the Agreement; and (b) Licensor's obligations under Section 7.5 of this Addendum are not subject to the Cap or to the exclusion of damages in Section 11.1 of the Agreement.
>
> **8.2 Precedence.** Notwithstanding Section 1.3 of the Agreement, nothing in this Addendum limits or reduces any liability of Licensor under Section 11.3 of the Agreement.

*Fallback, only if the client authorizes it:*

> a separate "super-cap" for data-protection liability equal to the greater of (i) $5,000,000 and (ii) three times the Fees paid in the 12 months preceding the claim, with DPA §7.5 breach-response costs sitting outside any cap and gross negligence, willful misconduct and fraud remaining uncapped.

**Negotiating leverage**

Laipeisk already carries $5,000,000 in cyber coverage, including breach response, notification, forensics and credit monitoring (COI Letter §2.1; Agreement §12.1(c)). Uncapped or high super-cap exposure is therefore insured risk for Laipeisk, and it is hard for Laipeisk to justify a one-year-fees cap.

**Client call:** confirm whether the DPA has been signed. Confirm the client's appetite for a super-cap fallback and at what floor. Get an estimate of the number of producers and records in the system so we can size the notification-cost exposure.

---

### Issue 2: The pending parent sale to Northfold requires Laipeisk's consent

**Location:** Agreement §16.2. The facts appear at SOW §1.2(b)–(c).

**What the documents say**

- **Agreement §16.2:** Bredeix may not assign without Laipeisk's prior written consent. The clause defines a Change of Control as "[a]ny *direct or indirect change in control* of Licensee, including any change in control of any entity that directly or indirectly controls Licensee, whether by merger, sale of equity…," and provides that it "shall be *deemed an assignment*." If a Change of Control occurs without prior written consent, Laipeisk "may terminate this Agreement on thirty (30) days' written notice."
- **SOW §1.2(b):** on August 28, 2026, the sole owner of Bredeix's parent, Bredeix Dairy Holdings, LLC, signed a Unit Purchase Agreement with Northfold Provisions Group. Closing is expected in Q1 2027.
- **SOW §1.2(c):** Laipeisk agreed to re-sequence the Phase 2 schedule around integration planning, but "[n]othing in this SOW constitutes Licensor's consent under Section 16.2."

**Analysis**

A sale of the equity of Bredeix's parent is an indirect Change of Control. It is therefore a deemed assignment requiring Laipeisk's prior written consent. No consent has been given, and the SOW expressly reserves the point.

The Agreement's no-waiver clause (§16.7) means Laipeisk's knowledge of the deal and its cooperation on scheduling will not amount to consent.

**Why it matters to Bredeix**

- **Operational risk.** HerdLedger runs Bredeix's milk procurement and, after Phase 2, its semi-monthly producer pay cycles, ACH payments, quality testing and hauling logistics. A 30-day termination right at or after closing would leave Bredeix unable to pay farmers or track milk quality on any realistic replacement timeline.
- **Timing.** Phase 2 production go-live is targeted for April 19, 2027, after the expected Q1 2027 closing. Bredeix would be mid-implementation, with $412,000 of Phase 2 fees in play, when the termination right arises.
- **Leverage for Laipeisk.** The consent requirement gives Laipeisk leverage to reprice or extract concessions just before closing. It could also cut across the purchaser's closing conditions or third-party-consent covenants in the UPA.

**Recommended fix**

Obtain Laipeisk's written consent (or an express waiver of the §16.2 termination right) now, well before closing. At the same time, amend §16.2 so that future affiliate reorganizations and acquirer transfers do not require consent.

*Proposed consent and waiver letter (to be countersigned by Laipeisk):*

> Laipeisk Systems, Inc. hereby consents, for purposes of Section 16.2 of the Software License and Services Agreement effective April 1, 2025, to the acquisition of Bredeix Dairy Holdings, LLC by Northfold Provisions Group (or its designated affiliate) pursuant to the Unit Purchase Agreement dated August 28, 2026, and to any resulting direct or indirect Change of Control of Bredeix Organic Creamery, LLC. Licensor irrevocably waives any right to terminate the Agreement, any Statement of Work, or the DPA by reason of that transaction, and agrees that the Agreement, each Statement of Work and the DPA continue in full force on their existing terms, without any change in Fees.

*Proposed amendment to Agreement §16.2 (insert after the first sentence):*

> Notwithstanding the foregoing, Licensee may, without Licensor's consent but on written notice, assign this Agreement to an Affiliate or to a successor to all or substantially all of the business or assets to which this Agreement relates, and no Change of Control of Licensee or of any entity controlling Licensee shall require Licensor's consent or give rise to any right of Licensor to terminate this Agreement.

If Laipeisk insists on a consent right, fallbacks include:

- consent "not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed," limited to transfers to a direct competitor of Laipeisk; and
- any post-closing termination right conditioned on at least 12 months' notice plus the §14.5 transition assistance at no charge.

**Client call**

- Confirm the expected closing date and whether the UPA treats this consent as a closing condition or covenant.
- Confirm whether the deal remains confidential beyond the disclosure already made in the SOW.
- Ask whether Northfold intends to keep HerdLedger or migrate Bredeix to its own systems. The answer directly affects how hard we push on Issue 4.
- Agree on sequencing: whether to bundle the consent request with the Issue 1 and Issue 4 asks or to secure consent first.

---

### Issue 3: The Phase 1 Rejection Notice was sent after the acceptance window

**Location:** SOW §2.2. The governing period is in Agreement §6.2.

**What the documents say**

- **Agreement §6.2:** Bredeix must deliver a written Rejection Notice "within ten (10) days after Delivery." If it does not, the Deliverable "is deemed accepted."
- **Agreement §5.2 and Schedule A:** milestone fees become payable on acceptance.
- **SOW §2.1:** Phase 1 Delivery occurred on **July 20, 2026**. The ten-day window therefore closed on **July 30, 2026**.
- **SOW §2.2:** Bredeix's Rejection Notice is "*dated August 7, 2026*," eight days late. The notice identified three nonconformities:
  - duplicate producer records created in the migration;
  - component test results (butterfat, protein, SCC) posting to the wrong producer accounts; and
  - organic premiums misapplied around certification renewal dates.
- Laipeisk contends the notice was untimely and the Deliverable accepted. Bredeix "disputes that the Phase 1 Deliverable has been deemed accepted and *reserves all rights*."
- The SOW does not extend the window, and under §1.3 the Agreement's ten-day period controls over the SOW in any event.

**Analysis**

On the face of the documents, the August 7, 2026 notice was untimely. Bredeix faces a credible deemed-acceptance argument and the resulting obligation to pay the Phase 1 milestone fee.

The point is still live, however, because Bredeix reserved its position and SOW §2.3 preserves each party's position. Bredeix has the following arguments and remedies:

1. **The ten-day clock may not have started on July 20.** "Delivery" is defined as Laipeisk's *written notice* that the Deliverable is installed and "ready for acceptance testing" (Agreement §1.1(e)). If no compliant written notice was given on July 20, or the Deliverable was not in fact test-ready, the clock may have started later.
2. **Warranty remedies survive acceptance.**
   - The Software Warranty (Agreement §8.2) runs "during the Term" and requires conformity to the Specifications. Laipeisk must correct a nonconformity within 30 days of notice, failing which Bredeix may terminate.
   - The Services Warranty (§8.3) requires re-performance of nonconforming Services if Laipeisk is notified within 90 days after performance. The August 7 notice falls comfortably within that period.
3. **Waiver or course of dealing.** Laipeisk has agreed to investigate the defects as part of Phase 2 data readiness (SOW §2.3). This argument is weakened by the no-waiver clause (Agreement §16.7), which requires waivers to be in writing, so it should not be the lead argument.
4. **Withholding payment.** Bredeix may withhold the Phase 1 milestone fee in good faith by written dispute notice under Agreement §5.3, pending resolution through the §15.2 escalation process.

**Why it matters to Bredeix**

- **The defects affect producer pay.** They go to the core of producer pay accuracy: duplicate producer records, component results posted to the wrong farm, and wrong organic premiums.
- **The defects will carry into Phase 2.** Phase 2 builds the payment module on this same master data. If Phase 1 is treated as accepted, Bredeix loses the clean §6.3–6.4 correction cycle, including the right after a third failed Delivery to a fee reduction or to terminate with a refund. Defects may then be baked into producer settlements and ACH payments.
- **Commercial consequences.** Mispaying organic premiums or component pricing exposes Bredeix to producer disputes and possible obligations under its producer contracts.

**Recommended fix**

Press the defect claims, keep the reservation of rights alive, and negotiate a written resolution that resets acceptance.

*Proposed SOW amendment (new SOW §2.4):*

> **2.4 Phase 1 Re-Delivery.** Notwithstanding Section 6.2 of the Agreement and any prior Delivery, the Parties agree that the Phase 1 Deliverable has not been accepted. Licensor shall correct the nonconformities identified in Section 2.2 and re-deliver the Phase 1 Deliverable no later than [date], whereupon the acceptance procedure in Sections 6.1 through 6.4 of the Agreement shall apply as if such re-delivery were the first Delivery. The Phase 1 milestone fee shall not be payable until acceptance of the re-delivered Phase 1 Deliverable. Deliverable D2-1 shall not be deemed delivered until the Phase 1 nonconformities are corrected.

*Proposed general fix to Agreement §6.2 (prospective, for Phase 2 deliverables):*

> Licensee shall notify Licensor in writing of any rejection within thirty (30) Business Days after Delivery. Failure to deliver a Rejection Notice shall not result in deemed acceptance unless Licensor has given Licensee a further written notice referring to this Section 6.2 and Licensee fails to respond within ten (10) Business Days after receipt.

In parallel, Bredeix should do two things:

- Send a written §8.2/§8.3 warranty notice covering the same three defects, so the warranty clocks run independently of the acceptance dispute.
- Send a §5.3 dispute notice for the Phase 1 milestone invoice, if it has been issued.

**Client call**

- Confirm whether and how Laipeisk gave written notice of Delivery on July 20, and why the notice went out on August 7.
- Confirm whether the Phase 1 Deliverable has been used in live production. Production use is itself acceptance under Agreement §6.5. If Bredeix is running live procurement on it, that undercuts the deemed-acceptance dispute and pushes us toward the warranty route.
- Confirm whether the Phase 1 milestone fee has been invoiced or paid, and its amount.

---

### Issue 4: Automatic five-year renewals with a 30-day opt-out window

**Location:** Agreement §14.2.

**What the document says**

On expiry of the three-year Initial Term (§14.1), the Agreement "shall renew automatically for *successive five (5) year Renewal Terms*" unless either party gives non-renewal notice "*not more than one hundred twenty (120) days* nor fewer than ninety (90) days before the end of the then-current term."

**Analysis**

- **Each renewal is longer than the original deal.** Every renewal commits Bredeix for five years, compared with a three-year original term.
- **The opt-out window is narrow.** It is only 30 days, and a notice sent either too early or too late is ineffective. Notices are effective only on receipt by courier or by hand (with email requiring a courier confirmation copy) (§16.1). New York courts enforce such windows as written.
- **There is no exit for convenience.** The Agreement has no termination-for-convenience right. Bredeix's only exits are for cause (§14.3), insolvency (§14.4), the warranty route (§8.2) or the subprocessor objection right (DPA §6.3).
- **The first window is close.** The Initial Term runs three years from April 1, 2025, ending on or about March 31, 2028. On a conservative calendar count, the first non-renewal window runs from about **December 2, 2027 to January 1, 2028**, over the holiday period. Because "three (3) years from the Effective Date" is ambiguous about whether the term ends March 31 or April 1, 2028, we should diarize to the earlier, narrower dates.

**Why it matters to Bredeix**

- **Loss of flexibility after the sale.** Post-closing, Northfold may want to standardize procurement and producer-pay systems across its group. A missed window would lock Bredeix into HerdLedger until about March 2033, with fee increases of up to 3% per year (§5.5).
- **Confused ownership during integration.** The renewal decision will fall in the middle of post-acquisition integration, when ownership of this contract and the notice address (§16.1, Attn: COO) may be in flux.

**Recommended fix**

*Proposed replacement Agreement §14.2:*

> **14.2 Renewal.** On expiry of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall renew automatically for successive one (1) year Renewal Terms, unless either Party gives the other written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days before the end of the then-current term. Licensor shall give Licensee written notice of the upcoming expiry and of Licensee's non-renewal right not less than one hundred twenty (120) days nor more than one hundred eighty (180) days before the end of the then-current term, and Licensee's deadline to give notice of non-renewal shall be extended to thirty (30) days after Licensee's receipt of that notice if Licensor fails to give it on time.

*Proposed new Agreement §14.7:*

> **14.7 Termination for Convenience.** After the Initial Term, Licensee may terminate this Agreement for convenience on ninety (90) days' written notice to Licensor, without penalty, and shall receive a pro rata refund of any prepaid subscription Fees for the period after termination. Section 14.5 (including transition assistance) applies.

Whatever is agreed, docket the non-renewal window now, with reminders at 180, 150 and 125 days before term end. Name an owner at Bredeix responsible for sending the notice by courier.

**Client call:** confirm whether Bredeix (and Northfold) wants a long-term commitment to HerdLedger. If so, Bredeix may be willing to trade a longer renewal for price protection. If not, termination for convenience becomes a priority ask.

---

## III. Insurance Certificate Cover Letter: no independent issue

I reviewed the COI Letter against Agreement §12. The coverage summarized matches the contractual requirements:

| Requirement (Agreement §12) | What the COI Letter shows |
|---|---|
| CGL of $1M per occurrence / $2M aggregate | Matches |
| Tech E&O of $5M | Matches |
| Cyber of $5M, including breach response and notification | Matches |
| Workers' compensation as required by law | Statutory coverage shown |
| Insurers rated A- VII or better | All insurers meet this |
| Bredeix as additional insured on the CGL policy | Named by blanket endorsement |
| 30 days' notice of cancellation or material reduction | Provided by endorsement |

I see no material issue. Three housekeeping points:

1. **Tail coverage.** The E&O and cyber policies are claims-made, with a January 1, 2019 retroactive date. Agreement §12.1 requires coverage for two years after the Term. We should confirm Laipeisk will keep these policies in force or buy tail coverage on expiry.
2. **The certificate is for information only (COI Letter §6.1).** If Bredeix wants comfort that the cyber policy would actually respond to a producer-data breach, it should request the policy provisions Laipeisk offers to provide.
3. **Post-closing certificate holder.** After closing, Bredeix may want Northfold added as a certificate holder. The broker needs Laipeisk's instructions to do this (COI Letter §5.2).

As noted in Issue 1, the $5M cyber limit is useful leverage for restoring uncapped data-breach liability.

---

## IV. Points for a client call before we respond to Laipeisk

1. **DPA status and fallback (Issue 1):** Has the DPA been signed? Will the client accept a data-protection super-cap as a fallback, and at what floor? How many producer records are in HerdLedger?
2. **Northfold transaction (Issue 2):** Expected closing date. Whether the UPA requires this consent. Confidentiality constraints. Northfold's plans for HerdLedger. Whether to seek consent first or bundle it with the other asks.
3. **Phase 1 facts (Issue 3):** Form and date of Laipeisk's Delivery notice. Reason the Rejection Notice went out on August 7. Whether Phase 1 is in live production use (Agreement §6.5). Status and amount of the Phase 1 milestone invoice.
4. **Commercial horizon (Issue 4):** Whether Bredeix and Northfold want long-term lock-in, which determines whether we trade renewal length for price protection or insist on termination for convenience.
5. **Overall strategy:** Laipeisk holds leverage through the consent requirement and the Phase 1 fee dispute. Bredeix holds leverage through the $412,000 Phase 2 engagement and Laipeisk's existing insurance. We should agree with the client which concessions are must-haves (we suggest consent and the data-breach cap) and which are tradeable.

### Issue 1: The DPA overrides the data-breach carve-out and caps Laipeisk's breach liability at 12 months' fees

**Where:** DPA §8.1, read with Agreement §§1.3, 11.2 and 11.3(c).

**What the documents say**

- **Agreement §11.2** caps each party's aggregate liability at "the Fees paid by Licensee in the 12 months preceding the claim" (the "Cap").

**Why it matters to Bredeix**

- **The mutuality is illusory.** The clause is drafted as mutual, but only Laipeisk processes Personal Data. In practice it limits Laipeisk's exposure alone.

- **The legal exposure is real.** A breach would trigger notice obligations under the NY SHIELD Act (GBL §§899-aa/bb) and the Vermont Security Breach Notice Act (9 V.S.A. §2435). Bredeix runs receiving stations in both states. It also invites claims from producers, possibly including ACH-diversion fraud losses.
- **There is a relationship cost.** Bredeix's farmer-supplier relationships are its supply base. A payment-data breach is both a legal and a commercial event for Bredeix, while Laipeisk's exposure would stop at roughly one year's fees.
- **Laipeisk is already insured for more.** The COI Letter confirms Laipeisk carries $5,000,000 in cyber liability coverage, expressly including breach response, notification, forensics and credit monitoring. The current clause lets Laipeisk keep most of that insured layer for itself. That is a strong negotiating point.

**Recommended fix**

*Primary position:* strike DPA §8.1 and conform DPA §8.2:

> **8.1 Liability.** Section 11 of the Agreement applies to liability arising out of or relating to this Addendum. For the avoidance of doubt, any breach of this Addendum, and any Personal Data Breach caused by Licensor or its Subprocessors, constitutes a breach of Section 9 of the Agreement, and Licensor's liability for it, including under Section 7.5 of this Addendum, is excluded from the Cap and from Section 11.1 of the Agreement pursuant to Section 11.3(c) of the Agreement.

We should also tighten Agreement §1.3 so that the DPA cannot be used to reduce Licensee protections:

> ...the DPA (as to Personal Data, except that nothing in the DPA shall limit or reduce Licensor's liability or Licensee's rights under Sections 9, 10 or 11.3 of this Agreement), then this License Agreement, then any Statement of Work.

*Fallback (only if the client authorizes it; see Part IV):* a separate data super-cap of not less than the greater of (a) $5,000,000 or (b) five times annual Fees. It should sit outside and in addition to the general Cap. The DPA §7.5 costs and regulatory fines and penalties should remain uncapped, and the §11.1 consequential-damages exclusion should not apply to data-breach losses.

### Issue 2: The Northfold sale of Bredeix's parent is an indirect Change of Control requiring Laipeisk's prior written consent

**Where:** Agreement §16.2. The triggering facts are recorded in SOW §1.2(b)–(c).

**What the documents say**

- **Agreement §16.2** bars Licensee from assigning without Licensor's prior written consent.
- It defines "Change of Control" to include "[a]ny *direct or indirect change in control* of Licensee, including any change in control of any entity that directly or indirectly controls Licensee, whether by merger, sale of equity, sale of assets or otherwise." A Change of Control "shall be *deemed an assignment*."
- If a Change of Control occurs without prior written consent, "Licensor may terminate this Agreement on thirty (30) days' written notice."
- **SOW §1.2(b)** records that on August 28, 2026, the sole owner of Bredeix's parent, Bredeix Dairy Holdings, LLC, signed a Unit Purchase Agreement with Northfold Provisions Group, with closing expected in Q1 2027.
- **SOW §1.2(c)** states expressly: "Nothing in this SOW constitutes Licensor's consent under Section 16.2 of the Agreement."

**Result.** The sale of the units of Bredeix's controlling parent is a textbook indirect Change of Control. No consent has been given. Laipeisk has gone out of its way to preserve its position in the SOW, even while accommodating the deal in the Phase 2 schedule.

**Why it matters to Bredeix**

- **Laipeisk gains a termination right at closing.** Once the deal closes, Laipeisk could end the Agreement on 30 days' notice. HerdLedger runs Bredeix's core milk-procurement and farmer-supplier records today. After Phase 2 it will also run producer pay, quality tracking and hauling logistics.
- **The timing is bad.** Closing in Q1 2027 overlaps the Phase 2 schedule: D2-2/D2-3 on January 18, D2-4 on February 15, D2-5 on March 15, and go-live on April 19, 2027 (SOW §5.1). A 30-day exit in that window could disrupt semi-monthly producer settlements.
- **Laipeisk gains leverage.** Even if it never terminates, it can use the consent requirement to reprice the Agreement or extract concessions, for example on Issues 1 and 3.
- **The clause is one-sided.** Laipeisk may assign freely on notice in its own M&A transaction. Bredeix has no matching right.
- **The deal team may be exposed.** The UPA likely contains seller representations or closing conditions about material contracts and third-party consents.

**Recommended fix**

*Immediate (pre-closing):* obtain a written consent and waiver from Laipeisk before closing, ideally as part of this round of negotiations:

> **Consent to Change of Control.** Licensor hereby consents, for all purposes of Section 16.2 of the Agreement, to the acquisition of Bredeix Dairy Holdings, LLC (or its equity) by Northfold Provisions Group or any of its Affiliates under the Unit Purchase Agreement dated August 28, 2026, and to any resulting direct or indirect Change of Control of Licensee. Licensor irrevocably waives any right to terminate the Agreement or any Statement of Work, or to modify any Fees or other terms, by reason of that transaction.

*Going forward:* amend §16.2 to (a) permit assignment and Change of Control to an Affiliate or successor without consent, and (b) remove the termination right:

> Notwithstanding the foregoing, Licensee may assign this Agreement without Licensor's consent, on written notice, to an Affiliate or to a successor to all or substantially all of its business or assets to which this Agreement relates, and no Change of Control of Licensee shall require Licensor's consent or give rise to any right of termination, provided the assignee or successor (if any) assumes Licensee's obligations in writing.

At a minimum, consent should be "not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed," and there should be no termination right where the acquirer is not a Laipeisk competitor.

### Issue 3: Automatic five-year renewals with a 30-day opt-out window

**Where:** Agreement §14.2 (with §14.1).

**What the documents say**

- **Agreement §14.1** sets an Initial Term of three years from April 1, 2025. On our reading, the Initial Term ends on or about March 31, 2028.
- **Agreement §14.2** provides that the Agreement "shall renew automatically for *successive five (5) year Renewal Terms*" unless either party gives non-renewal notice "*not more than one hundred twenty (120) days* nor fewer than ninety (90) days before the end of the then-current term."

**Result.** The opt-out window is only about 30 days long. By my count it runs from approximately **December 2, 2027 to January 1, 2028**, which falls over the year-end holidays. We should confirm the exact dates once we settle how the term end is computed. A notice sent outside that window, whether early or late, is ineffective. New York courts generally enforce such windows as written, and there is no termination-for-convenience right to fall back on. Each renewal also commits Bredeix for five years, longer than the original three-year term.

**Why it matters to Bredeix**

- **The deal may change Bredeix's systems strategy.** After the Northfold transaction, Bredeix may be integrated into Northfold's procurement or ERP environment. The SOW itself notes the "integration planning expected to follow that transaction" (SOW §1.2(c)).
- **The cost of missing the window is high.** A missed window locks Bredeix in through roughly March 2033. Subscription fees could increase annually under §5.5.
- **The exits are narrow.** The only escape routes are for-cause termination (§14.3), insolvency (§14.4), and the narrow warranty-failure termination (§8.2).
- **The window is easy to miss.** Personnel and notice addresses may change after closing; §16.1 notices currently go to Bredeix's COO.

**Recommended fix**

Amend §14.2 to provide one-year renewals, a wide opt-out window, and a termination-for-convenience right:

> **14.2 Renewal.** On expiry of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall renew automatically for successive one (1) year Renewal Terms unless either Party gives the other written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days before the end of the then-current term. Licensor shall give Licensee written notice of the upcoming renewal date not less than one hundred twenty (120) days, and not more than one hundred eighty (180) days, before the end of each term.
>
> **14.7 Termination for Convenience.** After the Initial Term, Licensee may terminate this Agreement for convenience on one hundred eighty (180) days' written notice, without penalty, and shall receive a pro rata refund of any prepaid Fees for the period after termination. Section 14.5 (including transition assistance) applies.

We should also extend §14.5 transition assistance from 90 to 180 days, given how hard it is to migrate producer-pay data.

*Internal action:* whatever is negotiated, we should diarize the non-renewal window now. That means calendar reminders at, say, 180, 150 and 125 days before March 31, 2028, sent to both the client and our docket.
